narrative.summary: On a transatlantic voyage, Neville Fairweather is found stabbed in his cabin. Witnesses report seeing him alive on the first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight at night. However, the ship's crew log records the steward Ferdinand Carrick leaving the crew quarters at ten minutes past eight. Investigations reveal a carefully staged impersonation exploiting social expectations and witness cognitive bias. The real murder occurred earlier, and the figure seen was an impersonator in a steward's uniform. Detective Katherine Bellamy unravels the deception, revealing the true culprit.

accepted_facts: Neville Fairweather was stabbed with a dagger to the heart in his cabin.
Witnesses saw a figure resembling Neville on the first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight at night.
Ferdinand Carrick was recorded leaving the crew quarters at ten minutes past eight at night.
A torn inch and a half fabric edge was found on Neville's cabin doorframe, matching steward uniform fabric.
Crew logs show Ferdinand's movements contradicting witness testimonies.
The first-class guest noted Ferdinand's unusual nervousness that evening.
inferred_conclusions: The figure seen on the promenade deck was an impersonator wearing a steward's uniform.
Neville was already dead by ten minutes past eight at night.
Ferdinand Carrick used his knowledge of ship procedures and access to impersonate Neville.
The torn uniform fabric proves the impersonation occurred at the victim's cabin.
Witness cognitive bias and social conventions misled multiple passengers.
Ferdinand’s alibi window excludes the real time of death, implicating him.

mechanism.description: The culprit, Ferdinand Carrick, exploited strict class segregation and social expectations by impersonating the victim, Neville Fairweather, on the first-class promenade deck. Witnesses misidentified the steward in uniform as Neville due to his customary attire and mannerisms. This cognitive bias was reinforced by the impossibility of crew presence on first-class decks and the victim’s known habits. The mechanism falsified the apparent time of death by staging the victim's presence at twenty minutes past eight at night, while the actual murder occurred at ten minutes past eight, as recorded by the crew log. The concealment relied on a torn piece of the steward's uniform found snagged on the victim’s cabin doorframe, and the discrepancy between witness sightings and log times.

delivery_path.step: Ferdinand dons a steward's uniform identical to Neville's usual attire.
He mimics Neville's mannerisms and appears on the first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight.
Witnesses see and report the figure as Neville, reinforcing the false identity.
Meanwhile, Neville is stabbed in his cabin at ten minutes past eight.
The torn uniform fabric is left snagged on the victim's cabin doorframe during the impersonation.

false_assumption.what_it_hides: The figure was actually Ferdinand Carrick impersonating Neville, allowing the real murder to occur earlier and remain unnoticed.

discriminating_test.design: By reconstructing the exact movements from the crew log and witness testimonies, and presenting the torn uniform fabric and dagger disturbances, the test demonstrates that only Ferdinand Carrick could have impersonated the victim on the promenade deck and accessed the murder weapon in the crew quarters, exposing the impossibility of other suspects' involvement.

Step 4: The glove smudge on the dagger (mid) exonerates Lavinia. All clues are presented before the discriminating test, ensuring logical deduction.
